sections.text: Speak not this to one who has not practised austerities, or to him who does not love, or who will not listen, or who mocks.
But he who teaches this great secret to My devotees, his is the highest devotion, and verily he shall come unto Me.
Nor is there among men any who can perform a service dearer to Me than this, or any man on earth more beloved by Me than he.

Discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasa Yoga -- Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. We are at the conclusion of Bhagavad Gita, and in this chapter Bhagawan has stated a few simple facts which we already know. We have discussed them before and also experienced them in our life. Something as simple as this: in this world, people have different temperaments. Not all people are alike. Each one has his or her own temperament. Depending on that temperament, he may be good at one thing or another. Everybody is not good at everything, but depending on your temperament, you may be good at something.
And also this temperament will make you like some things and dislike other things. So this temperament is your own nature or your personality. Therefore, because in this world the different people have different personalities, different temperaments, they do different things. Some are good at scholarly pursuits and some are good at doing heroic things and some are good at creating wealth and some are just happy serving others, you may find yourself to be somewhere in this spectrum. Not everybody likes same type of coffee. Some like strong, some like very mild.
Others may be somewhere in between. So you will find yourself somewhere in the spectrum of temperament. Some are very sattvic, some are very tamasic and most of us are somewhere in between. Therefore find out what your real nature is. Bhagawan said this is a fact that each one has his or her own qualities and temperaments. So depending on your temperament, now you have to find the field of activity which is appropriate for you.
So earlier in chapter three, Bhagavan said Swadharma Nidhanam Shreya Paradharma Bhayavahah -- working in your own nature is better, because anothers dharma is frightening. If you try to do something against your nature, it will be very frightening. You will always be a fish out of water. You are a very artistic person and you want to run a business -- you will be a fish out of water.
You will not feel comfortable. So therefore find your own Dharma and then work in it. So in this chapter again he reminds us what is good for you. So he said that Sriyan Swadharmo Vigunaha, Paradharma, Swanushti daat. Your Dharma alone is good for you, even though it has faults. It may not be as pristine as others, but this is what your nature is and it is good for you.
And therefore Sahajam, Karma, kaunteh. So find the field of activities which come naturally to you. Do the activities which come naturally to you. You shall not incur any sin in doing so. You shall not incur any sin. Continue doing what you like, what comes naturally to you.
And do not worry about whether Ill incur any sin or Ill incur any wrong tendencies. We have learnt in the previous chapter that no matter what your tendencies are and what activities you are performing, you start with Om Tatsat, purify them. So in chapter 17 we have learned that no matter what your Saddha is, whether it is Sattvic, whether it is, whether it is Raja Sikh, whether it is Tamasic, you are acting in that manner. But rather than worrying about whether it is Sattvik, Rajasik, or Tamasik, do whatever is natural to you. But whatever you do, start with Aum. Every activity which you do, remember him, that he is almighty and all pervading.
And he is enabling me to do this activity. So start with Om and say end with Tat, that this is not for me, this is for you. There is nothing that I am doing it for myself because I am not even capable of doing anything. He is all pervading and everything I am doing, I am offering to him because he made me do this. So Bhagawan said, with that attitude, when you perform any actions in the field of your liking which come naturally to you, you will find your happiness. We try everything and we get frustrated.
Thats because we say, one, you are not pursuing your own Dharma and secondly, you think you are doing it for yourself. Those two things, if you correct them -- find the field of activities which is natural to you, and then dont expect anything from it -- Then Bhagavan said that you will be relieved from these sorrows and unhappiness. In spite of all this diversity which we see in this world, there is a profound unity. Iswarahas, Sarvabhutanam, Prudeshe, Arjuna, Tisthati.
He said, this is why you should offer everything to him and remember him all the time. Even though you find yourself to be very different from others, even though you find all these people are very different from each other, theres one thing very common. They are all functioning because of that one single principle functioning through them. There are not several consciousnesses -- mine different from yours, yours different from hers, hers different from his. One consciousness functioning through all. Depending on the quality of the equipment, outer behavior will be different from each other.
Just as we have used these examples many many times. This room space is dependent on the conditioning. How far the walls are from each other and how far the ceiling is from the floor. But the space is the same space as it is outside. The space outside and space inside is no different same. All pervading space is in each room in this universe.
Wherever you find a space which is confined by limitations, the space is universal. The same way, Isvara Sarva Bhutanam Hrudeshe Tishtati -- the core of all being is the Ishvara himself residing there. Because of his presence only, things are functioning. But how are they functioning? Bhramayan Sarva Bhutani Yantra Rudhani Mayaya -- by his illusive power Maya, everyone is functioning in this world.
They are functioning because of Iswaras presence and his power of Maya. The elusive power Brahmayan Sarvabhoot are Yantra Rudhani. It seems like they are just mounted on a machine, helpless to act in this world. We are driven by our own likes and dislikes and vasanas almost compulsively. Whether we like it or not. We see something which is of our liking, we will be attracted towards it.
Something which is of not conducive, we will be staying away from it. Bhagavan said everybody is propelled by this Maya as if they are helpless. But at the core of all being, Ishvara is the cause for all beings functioning in this world. Keep that unity in mind. So this is a profound revelation. We knew that everybody is different from each other.
Everyone has their own qualities. Everyone has their liking and disliking. Everyone has their own talents. But see, what is common is the cause for all the talents and all the liking and all the disliking is that all pervading principle. The Ishvara, the Lord himself. So Brahman, the all pervading self, with his power of Maya becomes the almighty Creator Ishwara.
With this Maya, he creates this world of plurality. So I myself, with my power of dreaming, I create my own world of dream. While Im dreaming, Im by myself. Even the dream is me. The people in the dream is me. In the dreamer himself is also me.
There is no other entity. Only when I wake up, I realize that there are not too many people around. There were no different sceneries around. So this is like it is in Ishwaras mind, a great dream. So therefore he said Brahmayan Sarva Bhutani Yantra Rudhani Maya. By this elusive power of Ishvara, each individual in this world is functioning compulsively.
Driven by their own temperaments and qualities. So therefore he says Tamevasharanam gacha. So now the advice, having understood that people will be different: you are different from everybody else. Do not try to compare yourself with others and dont try to copy them. You find your own bearings, what is good for you, what you like.
Continue functioning, but keep the Lord in mind -- that he is Almighty. He is making me do all these things and therefore I am offering everything I do to Him. Tamevasharanam gacha. Take refuge in that Ishvara, that Almighty, all-pervading consciousness. Sarva bhavena Bharata -- in all your being, with all your thoughts, whether thinking about your professional life, your relationships, everything.
While you are thinking, put him in the center of it -- all these things are only possible because of Him. Take refuge in him that you are the ones who is enabling me to function in this world as an individual. Tat Prasada paramsanthim Sthanam prapsi Saswatam. If you take refuge in him with all your being, with all your thoughts, no matter what that is, offer it to him that I can only think this way because of you. I can only act this way because of you. Once you start assigning all credits to him, then you are relieved.
You have no responsibilities. So in the end Bhagavan said this individualized ego which is identifying with this body, mind and intellect and taking credit for what Im doing, thinking that Im the doer. If you just keep that aside, do everything that you are doing right now exactly as you are doing. Because you are doing it as per your nature. You are propelled by your nature to do it. If you try to resist your nature, it creates distortion, a kind of mental disease.
So keep doing what you are doing. Just keep in mind Tamevasharanam Gacha, Sarva Bhavya Bharata. Just take refuge in Him. Make your identification with him versus this limited body, mind and intellect. Tat prasadat paramshantin sthan praapasi Saswatam. The grace is when the identification is complete then I obviously become one with him, his qualities become my qualities.
I start thinking, I now have access to his capacities. You joined a company a day before, and from the next day onwards youre part of the company -- all the resources of the company are yours. You take the brochure of the company and go to a new client and say, I represent IBM. All of IBMs resources are your resources. But before that, a day before, when you had not joined the company yet, you didnt have that brochure from IBM.
You are just an individual. You can say, I can do this, and that doesnt really mean much. Once you attach yourself to the resources of the Great, all his resources become your resources; all the qualifications of that company become your qualifications. Once you identify with him and take refuge in him Tat Prasad with his grace you will achieve that Santisthanam Propyasi Sastvatam. You will find that eternal peace and a firm abode. All you have to do is just take refuge in him and continue doing what you are doing as per your own nature.
Itite Gnanam Akhyatam Guhyat Guhyatram Maya Vimrushyat Ashe. We have discussed this thing in detail from chapter two onward. We have analyzed every point. In the end I came down and told you: just follow your own Dharma, your own nature. You will not incur any sin.
Do not worry about what other people are doing, do not copy them. Your welfare is in following your own Dharma and giving up your ego and attachment. And I will take care of everything else. I told you this very secret of knowledge. Secret means it was hidden from you. It was right there but hidden from you.
Because of my own likes and dislikes, my vasanas, my ignorance, I was not able to see this. I took that coverings away from you so that you can see the knowledge as is. I told you in its entirety. Vimrushya Etit Asena. Reflect on it in its totality. Dont take a verse here and there from Bhagavad Gita.

These verses address the transmission of knowledge. Verse 67 specifies to whom this teaching should NOT be given: na atapaskaya (one without discipline), na abhaktaya (one without devotion), na ashushrusha (one unwilling to serve/listen), and one who abhyasuyati (cavils or finds fault). This is not exclusion but wisdom - teaching reaches only those prepared to receive it. Forcing spiritual knowledge on unprepared minds creates neither understanding nor transformation.
Verses 68-69 describe the supreme service: teaching this knowledge to sincere devotees is the highest form of worship, and no one is dearer to Krishna than one who shares this wisdom. This is the concept of jnana-yajna - the sacrifice of knowledge. The study group movement embodies this teaching, recognizing that teaching multiplies understanding both for teacher and student.
Consider: What knowledge have you received that is meant to be shared? Not everyone is ready - verse 67s criteria apply. But among those who show discipline, devotion, and willingness to learn, you have something to offer. Today, reflect on one insight from your spiritual journey that has genuinely helped you. Identify one person in your life who might benefit and is ready to receive. The teaching need not be formal - a conversation, a recommended reading, a shared practice. The Gita promises that sharing wisdom with ready students is the highest devotion. What will you share, and with whom?
